accident_report:
(1) Vehicle Initialization
On a straight, flat, single-direction roadway with four lanes and a wide shoulder on the right (lane 1 being the rightmost), three vehicles are traveling under dry road conditions with good visibility.
V1 is traveling in lane 2 at 95 km/h, maintaining a steady गति and intending to continue straight.
V2 is ahead of V1 in the same lane (lane 2), at a distance of approximately 18 meters, traveling at 70 km/h due to cautious driving behavior despite clear conditions.
V3 is in lane 3, slightly behind V1 by about 10 meters, traveling at 100 km/h and intending to overtake vehicles in lane 2.
All vehicles are moving steadily at initialization, but V1 is following V2 at an insufficient distance given the speed difference.

(2) Scenario Development
As the scenario progresses, the large speed difference between V1 (95 km/h) and V2 (70 km/h), combined with the short following distance of 18 meters, reduces V1’s available reaction time. Despite good visibility and dry road conditions, V1 delays deceleration due to overreliance on perceived safe conditions.

V2 suddenly performs an emergency brake, decelerating sharply from 70 km/h to near 20 km/h within a short distance, without any external obstruction, likely due to overcautious behavior. This abrupt deceleration becomes the primary trigger for the interaction.

V1 reacts with a delayed emergency brake due to the short following gap and high relative speed. The braking force is strong, but the remaining distance is insufficient to fully avoid a collision. At the same time, V1 slightly steers left toward lane 3 in an attempt to evade V2.

This lateral movement directly affects V3, which is traveling in lane 3 at 100 km/h. V3 detects V1 encroaching into its lane at close range (less than 8 meters longitudinal gap) and immediately initiates hard braking. However, due to its higher speed and limited headway, V3’s deceleration is constrained.

The combined effects of V2’s emergency braking, V1’s insufficient following distance and evasive maneuver, and V3’s high speed and reduced reaction space create a tightly coupled dynamic conflict among the three vehicles.

(3) Result
The first collision occurs when V1, unable to fully decelerate in time, rear-ends V2 in lane 2 at a reduced speed. The impact happens before V1 can fully merge into lane 3, and before V3 reaches the conflict point.
The collision involves V1 and V2 only, resulting from the chain of interactions driven by large speed differences, close following distance, and sudden emergency braking.
